items.title: 10.5 Balancing redox equations by the oxidation number method

source_refs.note: Topic 10.5 with Sample 10.4 and the Keep in Mind box, printed pages 217-219.

items: Write the skeleton equation of the redox reaction.
Identify the elements that change oxidation number during the reaction.
Record the oxidation numbers above the symbols of those elements.
Indicate the change in oxidation number by arrows joining the atoms on both sides; this shows the electrons gained or lost.
Equate the increase and decrease in oxidation number (electrons lost and gained) by multiplying with suitable digits.
Balance the rest of the equation by inspection (hit and trial).

blocks.title: Did you know and keep in mind
blocks.text: Inspection order: first balance all elements except N, O and H; then nitrogen; then oxygen; lastly hydrogen. If an element only rises or only falls in oxidation number, its species is written once on the right (Zn + HCl giving ZnCl2 + H2). If it both rises and falls (disproportionation), the species is written twice on the right, first for the increase then for the decrease (Cl2 + NaOH giving NaCl + H2O + NaOCl). If it changes and also stays unchanged, it is also written twice, first for the change then for no change (HNO3 + Cu giving Cu(NO3)2 + H2O + NO2; HCl + K2Cr2O7 giving Cl2 + KCl + CrCl3 + H2O).
Sample Problem 10.4: dichromate and hydrochloric acid

Skeleton: K2Cr2O7 + HCl giving Cl2 + KCl + CrCl3 + H2O. Oxidation numbers: K +1, Cr +6, O -2, H +1, Cl -1 on the left; Cl 0 in Cl2, Cr +3 in CrCl3. Chromium changes from +6 to +3 and is reduced (K2Cr2O7 is the oxidising agent); chlorine changes from -1 to 0 and is oxidised (HCl is the reducing agent). Half-reactions: K2Cr2O7 giving 2CrCl3 (reduction) and 2HCl giving Cl2 (oxidation). The decrease for Cr is 6 units per molecule of K2Cr2O7; the increase for Cl is 2 units per 2 molecules of HCl, so the oxidation half is multiplied by 3 to equalise 6 electrons: 6HCl giving 3Cl2. The equation becomes K2Cr2O7 + 6HCl giving 3Cl2 + KCl + 2CrCl3 + H2O. By inspection, 2KCl are needed; to balance Cl and K, 14 molecules of HCl are required, so 8 HCl are added to the left; to balance hydrogen and oxygen, 7H2O go on the right. Balanced: K2Cr2O7 + 14HCl giving 2KCl + 2CrCl3 + 3Cl2 + 7H2O.
Balance MnO2 + HCl giving MnCl2 + H2O + Cl2 by the oxidation number method.
